audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim Deborah-Barak-Jael prose narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Deborah as prophet/judge, Barak's summons, Sisera's chariots, Jael/Heber Kenite setting, Kishon battle, Sisera's flight, Jael's hospitality and killing, and defeat of Jabin.

verses.restored: Children of Israel again did evil in eyes of YHWH after Ehud died.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD, when Ehud was dead.

modern.text: After Ehud died, the Israelites again did evil in the sight of the LORD.

original.text: וַיֹּסִ֨פוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵה֖וּד מֵֽת

verses.restored: YHWH sold them into hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; commander of his army was Sisera, and he dwelt in Harosheth-hagoyim.

familiar.text: And the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor; the captain of whose host was Sisera, which dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles.

modern.text: So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his forces was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.

original.text: וַיִּמְכְּרֵ֣ם יְהוָ֗ה בְּיַד֙ יָבִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ כְּנַ֔עַן אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָלַ֖ךְ בְּחָצ֑וֹר וְשַׂר צְבָאוֹ֙ סִֽיסְרָ֔א וְה֥וּא יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בַּחֲרֹ֥שֶׁת הַגּוֹיִֽם

verses.restored: Children of Israel cried out to YHWH, for he had nine hundred iron chariots, and he oppressed children of Israel with force twenty years.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel cried unto the LORD: for he had nine hundred chariots of iron; and twenty years he mightily oppressed the children of Israel.

modern.text: Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, because Jabin had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he had harshly oppressed the Israelites for twenty years.

original.text: וַיִּצְעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֠י תְּשַׁ֨ע מֵא֤וֹת רֶֽכֶב בַּרְזֶל֙ ל֔וֹ וְ֠הוּא לָחַ֞ץ אֶת בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּחָזְקָ֖ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: Deborah, a woman, a prophetess, wife/woman of Lappidoth, she was judging Israel at that time.

familiar.text: And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time.

modern.text: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.

original.text: וּדְבוֹרָה֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה נְבִיאָ֔ה אֵ֖שֶׁת לַפִּיד֑וֹת הִ֛יא שֹׁפְטָ֥ה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא

verses.restored: She was sitting under Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in hill country of Ephraim, and children of Israel went up to her for judgment.

familiar.text: And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.

modern.text: And she would sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where the Israelites would go up to her for judgment.

original.text: וְ֠הִיא יוֹשֶׁ֨בֶת תַּֽחַת תֹּ֜מֶר דְּבוֹרָ֗ה בֵּ֧ין הָרָמָ֛ה וּבֵ֥ין בֵּֽית אֵ֖ל בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֵלֶ֛יהָ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַמִּשְׁפָּֽט

verses.restored: She sent and called Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali and said to him, Has not YHWH Divine of Israel commanded? Go and draw toward Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men from sons of Naphtali and from sons of Zebulun.

familiar.text: And she sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedeshnaphtali, and said unto him, Hath not the LORD God of Israel commanded, saying, Go and draw toward mount Tabor, and take with thee ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?

modern.text: She summoned Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, “Surely the LORD, the God of Israel, is commanding you: ‘Go and march to Mount Tabor, taking with you ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun.

original.text: וַתִּשְׁלַ֗ח וַתִּקְרָא֙ לְבָרָ֣ק בֶּן אֲבִינֹ֔עַם מִקֶּ֖דֶשׁ נַפְתָּלִ֑י וַתֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו הֲלֹ֥א צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֵ֤ךְ וּמָֽשַׁכְתָּ֙ בְּהַ֣ר תָּב֔וֹר וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ עִמְּךָ֗ עֲשֶׂ֤רֶת אֲלָפִים֙ אִ֔ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֥י נַפְתָּלִ֖י וּמִבְּנֵ֥י זְבֻלֽוּן

verses.restored: I will draw to you, to wadi Kishon, Sisera commander of Jabin's army, his chariots and his multitude, and I will give him into your hand.

familiar.text: And I will draw unto thee to the river Kishon Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will deliver him into thine hand.

modern.text: And I will draw out Sisera the commander of Jabin’s army, his chariots, and his troops to the River Kishon, and I will deliver him into your hand.’”

original.text: וּמָשַׁכְתִּ֨י אֵלֶ֜יךָ אֶל נַ֣חַל קִישׁ֗וֹן אֶת סִֽיסְרָא֙ שַׂר צְבָ֣א יָבִ֔ין וְאֶת רִכְבּ֖וֹ וְאֶת הֲמוֹנ֑וֹ וּנְתַתִּ֖יהוּ בְּיָדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Barak said to her, If you go with me, I will go; but if you do not go with me, I will not go.

familiar.text: And Barak said unto her, If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.

modern.text: Barak said to her, “If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ בָּרָ֔ק אִם תֵּלְכִ֥י עִמִּ֖י וְהָלָ֑כְתִּי וְאִם לֹ֥א תֵלְכִ֛י עִמִּ֖י לֹ֥א אֵלֵֽךְ

verses.restored: She said, I will surely go with you. Nevertheless the road on which you are going shall not be for your glory, for into hand of a woman YHWH will sell Sisera. Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.

familiar.text: And she said, I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the LORD shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.

modern.text: “I will certainly go with you,” Deborah replied, “but the road you are taking will bring you no honor, because the LORD will be selling Sisera into the hand of a woman.” So Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh,

original.text: וַתֹּ֜אמֶר הָלֹ֧ךְ אֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֗ךְ אֶ֚פֶס כִּי֩ לֹ֨א תִֽהְיֶ֜ה תִּֽפְאַרְתְּךָ֗ עַל הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה הוֹלֵ֔ךְ כִּ֣י בְֽיַד אִשָּׁ֔ה יִמְכֹּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶת סִֽיסְרָ֑א וַתָּ֧קָם דְּבוֹרָ֛ה וַתֵּ֥לֶך עִם בָּרָ֖ק קֶֽדְשָׁה

verses.restored: Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh; ten thousand men went up at his feet, and Deborah went up with him.

familiar.text: And Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh; and he went up with ten thousand men at his feet: and Deborah went up with him.

modern.text: where he summoned Zebulun and Naphtali. Ten thousand men followed him, and Deborah also went with him.

original.text: וַיַּזְעֵ֨ק בָּרָ֜ק אֶת זְבוּלֻ֤ן וְאֶת נַפְתָּלִי֙ קֶ֔דְשָׁה וַיַּ֣עַל בְּרַגְלָ֔יו עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אַלְפֵ֖י אִ֑ישׁ וַתַּ֥עַל עִמּ֖וֹ דְּבוֹרָֽה

verses.restored: Now Heber the Kenite had separated from Kenite, from children of Hobab father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent as far as oak of Zaanannim, which is near Kedesh.

familiar.text: Now Heber the Kenite, which was of the children of Hobab the father in law of Moses, had severed himself from the Kenites, and pitched his tent unto the plain of Zaanaim, which is by Kedesh.

modern.text: Now Heber the Kenite had moved away from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab the father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent by the great tree of Zaanannim, which was near Kedesh.

original.text: וְחֶ֤בֶר הַקֵּינִי֙ נִפְרָ֣ד מִקַּ֔יִן מִבְּנֵ֥י חֹבָ֖ב חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיֵּ֣ט אָהֳל֔וֹ עַד אֵל֥וֹן בצענים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶת קֶֽדֶשׁ

verses.restored: They told Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.

familiar.text: And they shewed Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam was gone up to mount Tabor.

modern.text: When Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up Mount Tabor,

original.text: וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לְסִֽיסְרָ֑א כִּ֥י עָלָ֛ה בָּרָ֥ק בֶּן אֲבִינֹ֖עַם הַר תָּבֽוֹר

verses.restored: Sisera called all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all people who were with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to wadi Kishon.

familiar.text: And Sisera gathered together all his chariots, even nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people that were with him, from Harosheth of the Gentiles unto the river of Kishon.

modern.text: he summoned all nine hundred of his iron chariots and all the men with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the River Kishon.

original.text: וַיַּזְעֵ֨ק סִֽיסְרָ֜א אֶת כָּל רִכְבּ֗וֹ תְּשַׁ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ רֶ֣כֶב בַּרְזֶ֔ל וְאֶת כָּל הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ מֵחֲרֹ֥שֶׁת הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֶל נַ֥חַל קִישֽׁוֹן

verses.restored: Deborah said to Barak, Rise, for this is day YHWH has given Sisera into your hand. Has not YHWH gone out before you? Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.

familiar.text: And Deborah said unto Barak, Up; for this is the day in which the LORD hath delivered Sisera into thine hand: is not the LORD gone out before thee? So Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.

modern.text: Then Deborah said to Barak, “Arise, for this is the day that the LORD has delivered Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone before you?” So Barak came down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men following him.

original.text: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ דְּבֹרָ֨ה אֶל בָּרָ֜ק ק֗וּם כִּ֣י זֶ֤ה הַיּוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁר֩ נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֤ה אֶת סִֽיסְרָא֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ הֲלֹ֥א יְהוָ֖ה יָצָ֣א לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַיֵּ֤רֶד בָּרָק֙ מֵהַ֣ר תָּב֔וֹר וַעֲשֶׂ֧רֶת אֲלָפִ֛ים אִ֖ישׁ אַחֲרָֽיו

verses.restored: YHWH threw Sisera into panic, and all chariots and all camp, by edge of sword before Barak. Sisera went down from chariot and fled on foot.

familiar.text: And the LORD discomfited Sisera, and all his chariots, and all his host, with the edge of the sword before Barak; so that Sisera lighted down off his chariot, and fled away on his feet.

modern.text: And in front of him the LORD routed with the sword Sisera, all his charioteers, and all his army. Sisera abandoned his chariot and fled on foot.

original.text: וַיָּ֣הָם יְ֠הוָה אֶת סִֽיסְרָ֨א וְאֶת כָּל הָרֶ֧כֶב וְאֶת כָּל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה לְפִי חֶ֖רֶב לִפְנֵ֣י בָרָ֑ק וַיֵּ֧רֶד סִֽיסְרָ֛א מֵעַ֥ל הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֖ה וַיָּ֥נָס בְּרַגְלָֽיו

verses.restored: Barak pursued after chariots and after camp as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and all camp of Sisera fell by edge of sword; not even one remained.

familiar.text: But Barak pursued after the chariots, and after the host, unto Harosheth of the Gentiles: and all the host of Sisera fell upon the edge of the sword; and there was not a man left.

modern.text: Then Barak pursued the chariots and army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and the whole army of Sisera fell by the sword; not a single man was left. Jael Kills Sisera

original.text: וּבָרָ֗ק רָדַ֞ף אַחֲרֵ֤י הָרֶ֨כֶב֙ וְאַחֲרֵ֣י הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה עַ֖ד חֲרֹ֣שֶׁת הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וַיִּפֹּ֞ל כָּל מַחֲנֵ֤ה סִֽיסְרָא֙ לְפִי חֶ֔רֶב לֹ֥א נִשְׁאַ֖ר עַד אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: But Sisera fled on foot to tent of Jael wife of Heber the Kenite, for peace was between Jabin king of Hazor and house of Heber the Kenite.

familiar.text: Howbeit Sisera fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite: for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.

modern.text: Meanwhile, Sisera had fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, because there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.

original.text: וְסִֽיסְרָא֙ נָ֣ס בְּרַגְלָ֔יו אֶל אֹ֣הֶל יָעֵ֔ל אֵ֖שֶּׁת חֶ֣בֶר הַקֵּינִ֑י כִּ֣י שָׁל֗וֹם בֵּ֚ין יָבִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ חָצ֔וֹר וּבֵ֕ין בֵּ֖ית חֶ֥בֶר הַקֵּינִֽי

verses.restored: Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me; do not fear. He turned aside to her into tent, and she covered him with rug/covering.

familiar.text: And Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said unto him, Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not. And when he had turned in unto her into the tent, she covered him with a mantle.

modern.text: Jael went out to greet Sisera and said to him, “Come in, my lord. Come in with me. Do not be afraid.” So he entered her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.

original.text: וַתֵּצֵ֣א יָעֵל֮ לִקְרַ֣את סִֽיסְרָא֒ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו סוּרָ֧ה אֲדֹנִ֛י סוּרָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י אַל תִּירָ֑א וַיָּ֤סַר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ הָאֹ֔הֱלָה וַתְּכַסֵּ֖הוּ בַּשְּׂמִיכָֽה

verses.restored: He said to her, Give me, please, a little water to drink, for I am thirsty. She opened skin of milk, gave him drink, and covered him.

familiar.text: And he said unto her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him.

modern.text: Sisera said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” So she opened a container of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלֶ֛יהָ הַשְׁקִינִי נָ֥א מְעַט מַ֖יִם כִּ֣י צָמֵ֑אתִי וַתִּפְתַּ֞ח אֶת נֹ֧אוד הֶחָלָ֛ב וַתַּשְׁקֵ֖הוּ וַתְּכַסֵּֽהוּ

verses.restored: He said to her, Stand at entrance of tent. If a man comes and asks you, saying, Is there a man here? then you shall say, No.

familiar.text: Again he said unto her, Stand in the door of the tent, and it shall be, when any man doth come and enquire of thee, and say, Is there any man here? that thou shalt say, No.

modern.text: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” he said, “and if anyone comes and asks you, ‘Is there a man here?’ say, ‘No.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ עֲמֹ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל וְהָיָה֩ אִם אִ֨ישׁ יָב֜וֹא וּשְׁאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְאָמַ֛ר הֲיֵֽשׁ פֹּ֥ה אִ֖ישׁ וְאָמַ֥רְתְּ אָֽיִן

verses.restored: Jael wife of Heber took tent peg and took hammer in her hand, came to him quietly, and drove peg through his temple, and it went down into ground; he was deeply asleep and weary, and he died.

familiar.text: Then Jael Heber’s wife took a nail of the tent, and took an hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground: for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died.

modern.text: But as he lay sleeping from exhaustion, Heber’s wife Jael took a tent peg, grabbed a hammer, and went silently to Sisera. She drove the peg through his temple and into the ground, and he died.

original.text: וַתִּקַּ֣ח יָעֵ֣ל אֵֽשֶׁת חֶ֠בֶר אֶת יְתַ֨ד הָאֹ֜הֶל וַתָּ֧שֶׂם אֶת הַמַּקֶּ֣בֶת בְּיָדָ֗הּ וַתָּב֤וֹא אֵלָיו֙ בַּלָּ֔אט וַתִּתְקַ֤ע אֶת הַיָּתֵד֙ בְּרַקָּת֔וֹ וַתִּצְנַ֖ח בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְהֽוּא נִרְדָּ֥ם וַיָּ֖עַף וַיָּמֹֽת

verses.restored: Look, Barak was pursuing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him and said to him, Go, and I will show you man whom you seek. He came to her, and look, Sisera fallen dead, with peg in his temple.

familiar.text: And, behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him, Come, and I will shew thee the man whom thou seekest. And when he came into her tent, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the nail was in his temples.

modern.text: When Barak arrived in pursuit of Sisera, Jael went out to greet him and said to him, “Come, and I will show you the man you are seeking.” So he went in with her, and there lay Sisera dead, with a tent peg through his temple.

original.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה בָרָק֮ רֹדֵ֣ף אֶת סִֽיסְרָא֒ וַתֵּצֵ֤א יָעֵל֙ לִקְרָאת֔וֹ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ לֵ֣ךְ וְאַרְאֶ֔ךָּ אֶת הָאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֑שׁ וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵלֶ֔יהָ וְהִנֵּ֤ה סִֽיסְרָא֙ נֹפֵ֣ל מֵ֔ת וְהַיָּתֵ֖ד בְּרַקָּתֽוֹ

verses.restored: On that day Divine subdued Jabin king of Canaan before children of Israel.

familiar.text: So God subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel.

modern.text: On that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites.

original.text: וַיַּכְנַ֤ע אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אֵ֖ת יָבִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ כְּנָ֑עַן לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Hand of children of Israel went on, going harder against Jabin king of Canaan, until they cut off Jabin king of Canaan.

familiar.text: And the hand of the children of Israel prospered, and prevailed against Jabin the king of Canaan, until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.

modern.text: And the hand of the Israelites grew stronger and stronger against Jabin king of Canaan until they destroyed him.

translation_notes: Deborah is explicitly prophetess and judge, publicly accessible under her palm. Her authority is not derivative of Barak and should not be minimized.
Eshet Lappidoth may mean wife of Lappidoth or woman of torches/flames; the phrase requires lexical and reception-history audit.
Barak's refusal to go without Deborah can be read as dependence on prophetic presence rather than simple cowardice; the narrative nevertheless shifts glory to a woman.
The Kenite setting is politically complex: Heber is linked to Moses' in-law people but at peace with Jabin's house, while Jael acts against Sisera inside her tent.

Jael's killing of Sisera uses hospitality, deception, and intimate domestic tools. It may be understood as resistance to an oppressor, but must not be generalized into approval of murder or domestic violence.
Sisera commands a system that oppressed Israel violently for twenty years, yet ethical reception still must resist glamorizing graphic killing.
The prose narrative prepares the poetic celebration in Judges 5, where war language becomes more vivid and morally harder.
safety_note: Do not use Judges 4 to deny women's spiritual authority, shame leaders who rely on prophetic partners, glorify assassination, or romanticize violence inside a home. Center Deborah's public leadership, the cry against oppression, Jael's agency under dangerous political conditions, and the refusal to turn liberation violence into a universal moral pattern.
